name: grep
description: Searches input for lines matching a pattern and prints them; the workhorse of text filtering on Linux.

about: grep interprets patterns as basic regular expressions by default: . any char, * repetition, ^/$ anchors, [abc] character classes. Use -E for +, ?, |, and groups without backslashes, or -P for Perl-compatible regex where supported. -F treats the pattern as a literal string and is the fastest option for fixed text.
useCases: Find text in files and command output.
Filter logs for errors and warnings.
Count occurrences and locate files containing a term.
mistakes: Patterns with spaces or special characters left unquoted: grep error: connection fails; use grep "error: connection".
Forgetting that grep matches substrings: grep "cat" also matches "category"; use -w for whole words.
warnings: grep on /dev, /proc, or binary files can produce "Binary file matches" noise or hang; use -a to force text or --exclude-dir to skip directories.
distroNotes: GNU grep supports -P (PCRE) and --include/--exclude patterns. BSD grep historically lacks -P; ripgrep and ag are popular faster alternatives but are third-party tools.
